links.outcome: Model discrimination across high versus moderate/low Charlson Comorbidity Index subgroups
links.effect: Discriminative ability remained robust across both CCI groups despite differing volumes of laboratory data and missing values.
links.quote: The discriminative ability of the model remained robust across both groups, implying that the clinical context of missingness outweighed the raw quantity of available data.

links.outcome: Performance in subgroups with more missing laboratory data (moderate/low CCI)
links.effect: Moderate/low-CCI patients had more missing data, but within event cohorts missingness patterns were similar and model discrimination stayed robust.
links.quote: Within the event cohorts, however, the high-CCI and moderate/low-CCI groups showed similar proportions and patterns of missing values.

unlisted_practices: Preserving real-world laboratory ordering patterns (informative missingness) rather than imputing or forcing complete inputs for early warning models

screen.reason: Retrospective study evaluating the performance and robustness of a deep learning-based early warning system (VitalCare-Major Adverse Event Score) across patient subgroups with different data missingness patterns.
